title: 10 Blocks Off Campus, One Reason Each
description: Explore the essential streets and corridors surrounding Auburn University, from the historic Toomer's Corner to the bustling student housing districts.

cards.title: The Gateway to Downtown
cards.subtitle: Intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street
cards.notes: Visit the historic intersection where campus meets the city to celebrate major athletic victories by rolling the iconic oak trees with toilet paper.
cards.short_summary: The historic intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street serving as the primary gathering spot for Auburn victory celebrations.
cards.evidence_claim: Toomer's Corner is a street corner located at the intersection of Magnolia Avenue and College Street, marking the northeastern-most reach of the campus and the beginning of downtown.
cards.source_title: A brief history of Rolling Toomer's Corner & Toomer's Drugstore - Auburn-Opelika Tourism
cards.access_notes: Public intersection accessible 24/7; Toomer's Drugs typically closes by 6:00 PM or 7:00 PM.

cards.title: The Student Living Corridor
cards.subtitle: West Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Walk this major thoroughfare to find high-density student housing complexes and popular local eateries like Momma Goldberg's Deli.
cards.short_summary: A primary east-west corridor lined with modern student apartment complexes and long-standing local businesses.
cards.evidence_claim: West Magnolia Avenue is home to several major student housing developments including 320 West Mag and The Magnolia at Auburn.
cards.source_title: Location | Student Apartments Near Auburn University | The Mill
cards.access_notes: Public street with various business hours; generally active late into the evening due to student housing.

cards.title: The Downtown Retail Hub
cards.subtitle: North College Street
cards.notes: Browse local boutiques and bookstores along this central downtown block, which serves as a primary shopping destination for students.
cards.short_summary: The main north-south commercial artery of downtown Auburn, featuring a high concentration of retail shops and restaurants.
cards.evidence_claim: North College Street features prominent local businesses such as Toomer's Drugs and J&M Bookstore, serving as a hub for student retail.
cards.access_notes: Public sidewalk access 24/7; most retail shops open 10:00 AM to 6:00 PM.

cards.title: The Parkside Connection
cards.subtitle: South Gay Street
cards.notes: Follow this street south from downtown to reach Town Creek Park, a popular off-campus green space for walking and relaxation.
cards.short_summary: A street connecting the downtown core to residential areas and significant municipal parks used by the student population.
cards.evidence_claim: Town Creek Park is located at 1150 South Gay Street and is described as a go-to spot for students needing to clear their mind.
cards.source_title: 7 places every college student loves in Auburn | The Bama Buzz
cards.access_notes: Public street; Town Creek Park is open from dawn to dusk.

cards.title: The Modern Residential Block
cards.subtitle: West Glenn Avenue
cards.notes: Observe the rapid development of luxury student housing like UNCOMMON Auburn along this busy northern edge of downtown.
cards.short_summary: A major thoroughfare north of campus that has become a focal point for new multi-story student apartment developments.
cards.evidence_claim: West Glenn Avenue is the site of several new student housing projects, including UNCOMMON Auburn at 250 W Glenn Ave.
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential buildings require keycard access for entry.

cards.title: The Campus-Adjacent Link
cards.subtitle: Wright Street
cards.notes: Walk this short connector street between Glenn and Magnolia to access several new student housing complexes within steps of the campus core.
cards.short_summary: A north-south street located directly adjacent to the university's northeastern boundary, undergoing significant residential redevelopment.
cards.evidence_claim: Landmark Properties purchased a site on Wright Street between West Glenn and Magnolia avenues for a new student housing community.
cards.source_title: New 825-bed student housing apartment coming to downtown Auburn | The Bama Buzz
cards.access_notes: Public street; heavily used by pedestrians walking to the Harbert College of Business.

cards.title: The Downtown Dining Row
cards.subtitle: East Magnolia Avenue
cards.notes: Explore a variety of local restaurants and cafes, such as Hamilton's on Magnolia, located just east of the Toomer's Corner intersection.
cards.short_summary: The eastern portion of Magnolia Avenue featuring a mix of upscale and casual dining options popular with students and visitors.
cards.evidence_claim: East Magnolia Avenue hosts several local hotspots including Hamilton's on Magnolia at 174 E Magnolia Ave.
cards.source_title: Location | Student Apartments Near Auburn University | The Mill
cards.access_notes: Public street; restaurant hours vary, with many serving lunch and dinner daily.

cards.title: The Southern Commercial Strip
cards.subtitle: South College Street
cards.notes: Visit this busy corridor for essential student services, including the Alumni Hall retail store and various fast-casual dining options.
cards.short_summary: A major north-south thoroughfare south of Toomer's Corner that provides critical commercial services to the university community.
cards.evidence_claim: South College Street is lined with local eateries and shops, including Alumni Hall at 339 South College Street.
cards.source_title: How to Find Off-Campus Housing Near Auburn University - Apartments.com
cards.access_notes: Public street; retail hours typically 10:00 AM to 7:00 PM.

cards.title: The Urban Living District
cards.subtitle: North Gay Street
cards.notes: Find high-rise student living options like The Standard at Auburn, located just a few blocks north of the downtown commercial center.
cards.short_summary: A street north of the downtown core that has seen significant development of mid-rise student apartment buildings.
cards.evidence_claim: The Standard at Auburn is located at 234 N Gay St, providing upscale student living near the heart of campus.
cards.source_title: The Standard at Auburn: Auburn Off Campus Housing
cards.access_notes: Public street; residential complexes are private with secure entry.

cards.title: The Residential Transition
cards.subtitle: East Samford Avenue
cards.notes: Travel east along this avenue to see the transition from campus-adjacent housing to established residential neighborhoods and local schools.
cards.short_summary: An east-west street that connects the southern edge of the downtown area to residential districts and community facilities.
cards.evidence_claim: East Samford Avenue is home to community landmarks like the East Samford School and various apartment complexes.
cards.access_notes: Public street; primarily residential and school zone.
